seen_animation: A single black-line apple with a stem and a hatched leaf sits between two grey line drawings of hands (a raised open hand at left, a lower hand with curled fingers at bottom right) and two grey diagonal lines at top. In frames 1-4 the apple moves slightly right and down. In frames 5-8 it moves down and left, lowest around frames 6-8. In frames 9-12 it drifts back up and to the right. In frames 13-16 it moves slightly down-left again. The apple stays upright the whole time, with the leaf always pointing up-right; its size and outline barely change. The grey hands and lines do not move at all.
seen_film: Close shot of a man's two hands in front of a tweed jacket holding an apple. In frames 1-4 the right hand grips the apple over the top while the left hand cradles it. In frames 5-8 the apple is lowered and turned in the fingers, and the right thumb works at its surface. In frames 9-12 the apple is held lower and rotated so a different side faces the camera; by frame 12 the top/stem area turns toward the viewer with a dark patch visible. In frames 13-16 the apple is turned further, appears smaller, and sits lower and slightly left, pinched between thumb and fingers, with the hands closing around it. The hands move and change grip throughout.
named_subject: An apple (with stem and one leaf)
evidence: The film shows the apple being turned in the hands: f.png 1-8 show the blemished side facing camera, f.png 33-40 show the apple rotated so the stem cavity and a dark patch face up-right, and f.png 45-49 show the apple lowered, smaller and viewed end-on between the fingers. In e.png the apple never rotates: the stem and leaf point up-right in every frame 1-49, and the outline is the same upright silhouette throughout. Position partly follows: e.png 1-22 the apple drifts down-left as in f.png 1-22, and e.png 30-40 it rises to the right while the film apple moves right in f.png 33-40. At e.png 45-49 the film apple drops lower and shrinks while the animated apple stays the same size and height. The grey hand drawings are fixed in every e.png frame while the film hands change grip continuously. Consecutive frames in e.png show small, even shifts with no doubling; the g.png path is compact and continuous with no large gaps. Judged from still frames only, not playback.
primary_gap: The apple only slides around upright while the film's event is the apple being turned over in the hands, so the rotation and the lowering/shrinking at the end (f.png 33-49) are missing.
closes_when: Across e.png 30-49 the stem and leaf swing from top toward the viewer and then out of view as the apple tips, and in e.png 44-49 the apple sits lower and slightly smaller between the grey hands, matching f.png 44-49.
protect: The apple drawing matches c.png exactly (lumpy rounded outline, notched two-lobe bottom, straight stem, single hatched leaf, thin even stroke); frame-to-frame motion is small and even with no pops or doubling; the apple is placed between the two hands at about the same screen position as the film apple.
identity_gap: The animated apple keeps c.png's outline, notched base, stem and hatched leaf with the same thin stroke, so it reads as the same drawing.
